title: 夜市为什么让人念念不忘
title_en: Why Night Markets Stay in the Memory
summary_zh: 白天的停车场，晚上摇身一变成了夜市。便宜的小吃、热闹却不吓人的气氛、看得见的手艺，让旅行者记得最久的往往是这里。读完你能用被动语态和对比句介绍一个热闹的地方。
body: As the sun goes down in many cities, car parks and quiet side streets change their job. Folding tables appear, strings of bulbs are hung between lamp posts, and within an hour a night market is in full swing. For visitors, these markets are often the most memorable part of a trip, and it is worth asking why. Part of the answer is the food, which is cooked in front of you and usually costs very little. You can try five or six small dishes instead of committing to one large meal, so curiosity is rewarded rather than punished. But the atmosphere matters just as much. Night markets are crowded, noisy and slightly chaotic, yet they rarely feel threatening, because everyone is there for the same simple pleasures. Families share plates at plastic tables, students compare snacks, and older couples walk slowly as if they have followed the same route for decades. There is also a sense of performance. A vendor flipping pancakes at speed or pulling noodles by hand is putting on a small show, and the queue that forms becomes part of the audience. Unlike a restaurant, where the kitchen is hidden, a market lets you watch every step. Of course, night markets have their critics, who point to litter, noise and the problem of parking for local residents. Those concerns are fair, and the best markets handle them with clear rules and early closing times. Even so, for one evening they turn an ordinary street into a shared living room, which may be why travellers remember them long after the museums have blurred together.

knowledge.explanation: 被动语态 are hung，重点是“灯串被挂起来”，不关心是谁挂的。描写场景变化时很常用。

title: 一个背包旅行一周
title_en: A Week with Only a Backpack
summary_zh: 只背一个包出门一周，听起来很难，其实只要按「整套搭配」来带衣服、缩小洗漱用品、留一点空位就行。读完你会收拾一个轻便的行李，也能用 so that… 和动名词主语写出清楚的建议。
body: Travelling for a week with only a backpack sounds like a challenge for minimalists, but it is easier than most people think, and it changes the whole trip. Without a heavy suitcase, you can take stairs, jump on crowded buses and walk from the station instead of queuing for a taxi. The secret is to plan around outfits rather than individual items. Choose clothes in two or three colours that all go together, so that every top works with every pair of trousers. Three tops, two pairs of trousers or skirts, and one warm layer will cover most situations, especially if you can wash a few things on the way. Wear your heaviest shoes and jacket on the journey rather than packing them. Next, shrink your toiletries. Small refillable bottles take up far less room than full-size ones, and most basics can be bought at your destination if you run out. Electronics are often the hidden weight in a bag, so ask yourself whether you really need a laptop as well as a phone. Pack the things you will need first, such as tickets and a charger, at the top or in an outside pocket. Finally, leave a little empty space. A bag that is full on day one has no room for the souvenir you did not plan to buy, and you will end up carrying it in a plastic bag for the rest of the week. Once you have travelled light, a big suitcase can start to feel less like a convenience and more like a piece of furniture you have to take everywhere.

knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句：if 从句用一般现在时；主句 can be bought 是带情态动词的被动。
